 Since foods rich in calcium (primarily dairy products) are also high in phosphorus content 
and must be restricted; calcium carbonate and calcium acetate may be used between meals to 
increase serum calcium levels. The K/DOQI Clinical Practice Guidelines for Bone Metabolism and 
Disease recommends 1.5 to 2.0 g of calcium (including dietary and supplemental calcium) for CKD 
stages 3 and 4 and 1.5 to 1.8 g for stages 4 and 5 not yet on dialysis. Goals are to keep serum calcium 
levels within normal range.
Water Balance and Fluid Restriction
